cues.text: Welcome to the sound lab. There are three benches to explore: a ripple tank, an echo bench, and a ship's sonar. Predict, play with the controls, measure, and explain what you see.
This is the ripple tank, wired to an oscilloscope. You are about to change the frequency. First, predict what will happen to the wavelength.
Now for the amplitude. Before you turn it up, predict what would happen to the loudness if this were a sound wave.
Welcome to the echo bench. You will clap in the open field and then in the small room. Predict how the two will sound different.
Time for the cliff. Predict how far away it is. Then shout, and time the echo yourself with the stopwatch.
This is the ship's sonar. Predict the depth, send a pulse and read the timer. Then work out the depth from your own reading.
Last, the ultrasound scanner. You will compare a scan made with ordinary sound and one made with ultrasound. Predict why ordinary sound cannot be used for this.
Prediction locked. Now do what the checklist asks on the bench, then press run.
That is not what you predicted, and that is fine. Surprises are where the learning happens. Look closely, then explain what you saw.
Every task is run and explained. When you are ready, press finish to see your summary.
Here is your summary. Look back at any prediction that surprised you, and think about why it turned out that way.
